contests.title: Initiative IP26-645 — State and local income taxes

big_picture.text: Washington passed a new income tax on the part of someone’s yearly income above $1 million, starting with 2028 income. Voters are deciding whether to cancel that tax before it begins and restrict other income taxes described in this measure.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Cancel that planned tax and put the measure’s income-tax restrictions into law. Other tax credits and exemptions created with the law would not be directly canceled by this vote.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Leave the planned tax and current rules in place, unless lawmakers or courts change them later.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters say a new state income tax could discourage business investment and make it easier to expand income taxes later. Their goal is to prevent that kind of tax from taking effect.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: Opponents want to keep a source of revenue mainly collected from very high incomes. They argue that removing it could make it harder to fund schools, health services, and other programs.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome.

who_affected.text: The planned tax is aimed at income above $1 million, not at everyone who makes a paycheck. State services and people who use them could be affected by future budget choices.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: State budget analysts estimate about $11.4 billion less revenue over five fiscal years if the measure passes. That is a forecast across several years, not money the state has already collected.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: Repealing the tax would also prohibit certain future income taxes under the measure’s terms. Future lawmakers could choose different taxes, spending cuts, or other changes in response to less revenue; this measure does not dictate which programs would lose money.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: One campaign used a $13 billion figure over a different time period. Do not compare that number directly with the state’s $11.4 billion estimate as if they measure the same years.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: Independent forecast replication, legal interpretation beyond the pamphlet, and future legislative responses have not been completed.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

contests.title: Initiative IL26-001 — Parental rights in public schools

big_picture.text: Washington changed its parental-rights school law in 2025. This initiative asks whether to return to the earlier 2024 version. The differences include when parents can see student records, what information schools share, and some notice and opt-out rules.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Bring back the earlier rules. For example, the proposed text generally sets ten business days for access to covered student records, instead of the longer period in current law.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Keep the newer version of this particular law. Other state and federal rules about parents, students, education, and privacy would still apply.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters want parents to know more about their children’s school experiences and receive covered records sooner. They believe parents need that information to guide their children and challenge school decisions.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: Opponents are concerned that broader access and notification rules could reveal sensitive information in situations where a student may need privacy or protection.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome.

who_affected.text: Parents, students, teachers, and school staff who handle sensitive student information could see changes to their rights or duties.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: The state estimates no major direct cost. Schools might have smaller costs to change forms or procedures; the exact amount is not known.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: Schools could have to change how staff handle requests and notifications. The consequences can differ for ordinary records and sensitive medical or child-protection situations; other privacy laws and the limited investigation exception still matter.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: The proposed text includes a limited exception involving some child-abuse investigations. The exact rules and other privacy laws matter; it is not accurate to say that there is no exception at all.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: Precise interactions with other disclosure, child-protection and education laws require separate legal review.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

big_picture.text: This proposal would change eligibility for certain girls-only sports teams in grades K–12. It would use the measure’s definition of biological sex and require verification by a health care provider.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Apply the new eligibility and verification rules. The state’s explanation says transgender girls would generally be excluded from the covered girls’ teams.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Keep the current eligibility system rather than add these new restrictions. That does not prevent future changes through other laws or school sports rules.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters argue the new eligibility definition would protect opportunities and competitive fairness for girls in the covered sports.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: Opponents are concerned about excluding transgender girls and about possible burdens, privacy problems and disputes when schools or providers verify eligibility.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome.

who_affected.text: Students who play covered interschool sports, their families, coaches, schools, and health care providers could be affected.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: The state estimates about $21,000 to update guidance, plus school costs it cannot yet calculate. This is not a complete estimate of every possible expense.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: The rules could change team participation, require provider paperwork and create school compliance work. Lawsuits or conflicts with other rules are possible but not certain; no comprehensive participation or health-cost estimate was verified.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: The proposal lists different ways a provider could verify eligibility; it does not require every listed test for every child. The official fiscal statement also has a timing inconsistency that has not been resolved.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: Implementation details, medical practice, litigation and participation estimates are not independently verified here.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

big_picture.text: County Council members help decide county budgets, services, and land-use rules. This amendment would limit how many terms they could serve in a row.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Allow up to three consecutive terms on the Council. Someone who sits out a full term could run again. Earlier consecutive service and a term served more than halfway would count under the proposal.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Do not add this new consecutive-term limit to the county’s main rules.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters believe a break after three terms would make more opportunities for new candidates and reduce advantages from long incumbency.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: Opponents argue that voters should be able to keep an experienced councilor without a forced break, especially if the person is doing work voters like.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome.

who_affected.text: People running for Council and voters who want to keep or replace an experienced council member would be affected.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: The official explanation does not provide a dollar cost or savings estimate.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: Term limits could increase turnover and reduce experience within the Council. They might also shift more institutional knowledge to unelected staff. Those possible effects have not been measured for this amendment.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: This is a limit on terms in a row, not a lifetime ban from Council.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: Historical tenure claims and predictions about governance quality are not independently checked.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

big_picture.text: The county passes a budget to decide how much money different services can use. This amendment would move important budget information and public discussion earlier in the year.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Require earlier steps, including preliminary budget information by August 31, a public presentation by September 8, and budget adoption by November 30 under the proposed schedule.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Keep the current budget-writing process rather than put these new dates in the Charter.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters want budget numbers and meetings earlier so residents and councilors can ask questions before the county adopts its spending plan.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: Opponents question whether a fixed schedule belongs in the Charter and whether extra steps or early estimates could increase work without improving decisions.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome. The schedule and any workload effect should be checked against actual budget operations.

who_affected.text: County departments, Council members, and residents who want to study or comment on spending would be affected.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: The official explanation does not calculate extra staff costs or savings.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: Earlier deadlines may improve public access but can create pressure to produce estimates before all information is available. This measure does not guarantee lower taxes or more public participation.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: Voting Yes would not itself raise taxes, cut spending, or guarantee more people will attend public meetings.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: Implementation cost and whether the revised schedule improves participation remain unverified.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

contests.title: Charter Amendment 21 — Board and commission appointments

big_picture.text: County boards and commissions advise on specific public issues. Right now, there are rules about who can suggest people to serve on them. This measure would expand that nomination role.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Allow both the County Council and County Manager to nominate people for more boards. The Council would still make the final appointments.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters want elected councilors as well as the County Manager to propose people for more county boards, while keeping final appointments with the Council.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: No formal opposing statement was located in the reviewed pamphlet. A possible question to examine is whether shared nomination authority would improve recruitment or complicate appointments.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome. The possible concern is an analytical question, NOT attributed to a submitted opposing committee.

who_affected.text: People who want to serve on county boards, and the officials who choose them, could be affected.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: The official explanation provides no estimated cost.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: The balance of influence over who is considered for county boards could change. That does not automatically change board decisions, and the Ethics Review Commission is excluded.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: The county Ethics Review Commission is specifically left out of this change.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: Actual recruitment benefits and governance effects have not been independently assessed.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

big_picture.text: A primary election is an earlier round that can narrow a field of candidates. This amendment addresses certain county offices that are already nonpartisan, meaning the office is not elected under a party label.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Send a covered nonpartisan race directly to the general election when only one or two candidates file, following the amendment’s rules.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Do not add these changes to the county Charter; existing state and local election rules continue to apply.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters say holding a primary when no one needs to be eliminated wastes election money. They want a simpler election process.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: Opponents say the primary gives challengers and voters an earlier, publicly supported chance to learn about the candidates. They worry that skipping it could make incumbents better known than challengers.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome.

who_affected.text: Voters and candidates in the covered county offices would see a different election schedule in some years.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: Supporters say skipping some primaries could save money, but the official explanation does not give a verified dollar amount.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: The change could save some administration costs and reduce the number of appearances on primary ballots, while also shortening the period when these races appear on mailed ballots. Neither the savings nor effect on voter knowledge is established by the text alone.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: This does not turn partisan offices into nonpartisan ones, and it does not cancel every primary election.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: Actual savings and effects on voter knowledge or competition need separate evidence.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

contests.title: Charter Amendment 23 — County Manager annual report

big_picture.text: The County Manager already reports on county work. This amendment would make a yearly public report about the county’s money and activities an explicit Charter requirement.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Require an annual report, a public presentation, and broad public access to the information.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Do not add this new Charter requirement; other existing reporting duties remain.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters want a yearly report guaranteed by the Charter so residents can follow county money and activity rather than depend on officials choosing to publish one.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: No formal opposing statement was located in the reviewed pamphlet. A possible concern is whether a mandated report adds staff work or becomes a promotional document instead of useful public information.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome. The possible concern is an analytical question, NOT a reported opposing campaign position.

who_affected.text: Residents trying to understand county spending and the manager and staff who prepare the report would be affected.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: The explanation gives no fixed cost. It does not require an expensive printed mailing to every household.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: The Manager would have another required reporting step; publication could help scrutiny but could also consume staff resources. The proposal does not require printing and mailing it to every household.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: The rule says the report must be widely available, not that every person must receive it by mail.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: Publication method, actual costs and application of election-related restrictions need clarification.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

big_picture.text: Before passing some county-made rules that could affect housing, the county would have to study how those rules might change the number of homes, the land available, building permits, and the cost of construction.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Require a housing impact study before certain county-proposed laws with a direct, important effect on housing or development costs.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Do not add this study requirement to the Charter. The county could still study housing when it chooses or when another law requires it.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters believe a required housing-impact study would show tradeoffs before county leaders vote on rules that could make housing harder to build or afford.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: Opponents question whether another required study could slow needed county decisions, cost money or repeat analysis already done.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome.

who_affected.text: People building, renting, buying, or planning homes, along with county planning staff, could be affected.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: The official explanation provides no reliable total for the cost of the studies. Staff or outside experts could do the work.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: The process could give Council clearer evidence but also add staff work and time for some proposals. A completed study would not itself change rent, create homes or require the Council to follow its findings.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: Routine changes required by state law are excluded. A study requirement does not by itself create new homes or lower rent.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: Staff workload, consulting costs and effects on housing supply or affordability require separate assessment.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

contests.title: Charter Amendment 25 — Supermajority for certain taxes

big_picture.text: Today, the five-member County Council votes on county taxes under existing rules. This amendment would require a larger majority to approve certain newly levied taxes and increases to those taxes.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Require at least four YES votes out of five Council members for the taxes covered by this new two-thirds rule.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Keep the current voting requirement for those tax decisions.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters want a wider agreement on the Council—at least four of five members—before a covered new tax or increase can pass.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: Opponents are concerned that a higher vote threshold could let a smaller group of councilors block funding even when most councilors believe a service needs it.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome.

who_affected.text: County leaders planning new taxes and people who use county-funded services could be affected by future decisions.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: This vote does not cut an existing tax or change your bill right away. Any future money effect depends on what taxes the Council considers.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: The rule could change which future tax proposals pass and how county leaders negotiate budgets. It would not directly lower existing taxes and excludes several kinds of charges and renewals.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: Taxes already being collected on January 1, 2027 are excluded, as are certain renewals and fees. This is not a four-vote rule for every county charge.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: Application to a specific future tax action and future service effects need separate legal and fiscal review.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

big_picture.text: People can collect signatures to ask county voters to decide an issue. This amendment would change some of those petition rules, including how many signatures are needed.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Lower certain signature thresholds from 10% to 8% under a formula based on votes in the governor’s election. It would also change parts of checking signatures and create a way to bring smaller proposals before Council.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Keep the current county petition rules and signature thresholds.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters want to lower some signature requirements so residents can bring more ideas directly to government or voters.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: Opponents worry that lowering the bar may lead to more proposals, more election or verification work, and less support behind each one before it moves forward.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome.

who_affected.text: Residents who organize petitions, election workers who check them, and the County Council could be affected.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: Supporters expect savings from different signature-checking rules, but no independently confirmed dollar amount is provided.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: More petitions could reach county staff and Council; some could lead to ballot elections. An easier petition process would not guarantee a proposal becomes law, and mini-initiatives do not automatically go to the ballot.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: Eight percent does not mean eight percent of every county resident. A smaller mini-initiative can get a Council hearing without automatically becoming a ballot question.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: Signature-calculation examples, implementation savings and historical comparisons need separate verification.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

big_picture.text: A performance audit checks whether a program uses money well and meets its goals. This amendment would require a process for the County Council to arrange independent checks of county programs when needed.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Create that audit process and allow audits as needed. Outside contractors would have to follow specific selection and audit standards.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Keep the existing system rather than add this extra Charter process.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters want the legislative branch to be able to commission performance audits that look for waste, problems or improvements in county programs.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

critics_why.text: Opponents question the cost, duplication with existing oversight, and whether the Council needs another audit process.
critics_why.qualifier: Attributed original opposition or editorial question, not a guaranteed outcome.

who_affected.text: County departments, the Council, and residents who want to know how programs perform could be affected.
who_affected.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

money.text: Opponents have claimed high yearly costs; supporters say no yearly audit is required. Neither side’s cost claim has been independently established. Setting up or using the process could still cost money.
money.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

other_impacts.text: Audits may identify improvements and may also cost staff time or outside-contract money. The measure requires a process but does not require one paid audit every year; annual state-required audits remain separate.
other_impacts.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

one_to_remember.text: An audit process would be required, but a new paid audit every year would not. Existing state-required financial audits would continue.
one_to_remember.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

unresolved.text: The underlying fiscal analysis, scope, contracting choices and net savings need separate review.
unresolved.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

contests.title: County Proposition 12 — Public safety capital bonds

big_picture.text: Clark County wants to build or improve jail space, courtrooms, and Sheriff’s Office facilities. It would borrow money by selling bonds, which are loans paid back over many years with interest.
big_picture.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

yes.text: Let the county borrow up to about $366.2 million for those building projects and collect extra property taxes to repay the loans and interest.
yes.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

no.text: Do not approve this bond plan or the extra taxes tied to repaying it. That does not mean the buildings have no repair or space needs.
no.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.

supporters_why.text: Supporters want enough space and safer buildings for jail operations, courtrooms and the Sheriff’s Office. They argue that delaying construction could leave existing problems unresolved.
supporters_why.qualifier: Prepared, source-attributed analysis, not a completed independent legal/fiscal review.
